minutes.headline: Select Board recommended most FY2022 town meeting articles after hearing a clean FY2020 audit.
minutes.summary: The board heard the FY2020 audit, which carried an unmodified opinion and no new management letter comments. It then went article by article through the May 1 town meeting warrant, setting amounts and recommending approval or deferral, and worked through the language of the APDC override article. It also approved a drainage fix, revoked a fuel license, and signed the warrants.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend most May 1 town meeting warrant articles, including the budget, capital plan and stabilization deposits.
Several articles (4, 18-19, 26, 30, 31) were deferred to town meeting rather than given a recommendation.
After a long discussion of its language, the board recommended Article 24, the APDC override, as amended, with one abstention.
The board heard the FY2020 audit, which had an unmodified opinion and no new management letter comments, and the auditor suggested reviewing old ambulance receivables for write-off.
The board signed the annual town meeting warrant for May 1, 2021 and the town election warrant, and voted to revoke the fuel storage licenses at 416 Electric Ave.

why_it_matters: These recommendations shape the budget, capital plan and override question that voters will be asked to decide at the May 1, 2021 town meeting.
The audit and the discussion of free cash and stabilization show how much the town holds in reserve, which bears on how much of next year's spending falls on the tax bill.
watch_next: Annual town meeting on May 1, 2021, where the recommended articles, including the amended Article 24, come to a vote.
The deferred articles (4, 18-19, 26, 30, 31) and the road ownership and utility digging question sent to town counsel for a future agenda.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most Article recommendations, the Article 8 transfer of $250,000, the Article 5 and 6 totals and the sewer figure. They differ on votes recorded in only one record (Articles 15 and 27, the 3-2 Article 24 vote), on how Article 24 as amended came out, and on which articles were deferred. A reader should check the recording and the warrant for Articles 13/12/15 and for the deferral list (17, 30, 31) before quoting either record.
